title: The Pain–Comfort Lab: Looking Inside a Language Model
description:
A curiosity-driven, inquiry-based lab for beginners with basic machine-learning knowledge but no transformer experience. Across eight Jupyter notebooks (Google Colab ready), students take snapshots of an open language model's internal activations (Qwen2.5-1.5B), find a pain-to-comfort direction, test it against a sealed test set and controls (shuffled labels, random directions, a bag-of-words baseline), nudge the model along it (activation steering), and design their own investigation.

Every step includes code walk-throughs that show what each line returns, why each data structure and parameter was chosen, and how to inspect shapes. Includes a small labelled sentence dataset with a datasheet, a student worksheet, an instructor guide and a research-ideas guide.

The lab can show whether a model's internal numbers contain a pattern linked to pain-versus-comfort language; it cannot show that a model feels anything.

notes: Developed with assistance from generative AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) for code drafting, explanation revision, restructuring and testing; all content was reviewed by the author. The Qwen2.5-1.5B model is not included; it is downloaded from Hugging Face under its Apache 2.0 licence.
